sources.title: Nihongo no Mori
sources.ja: 日本語《にほんご》 の 森《もり》
sources.en: Japanese teachers explain JLPT grammar, vocabulary and reading in Japanese, with playlists arranged by level.
sources.tip: At N3 and above, pick the playlist for your level and watch one lesson twice: first for the idea, then pausing to say the examples aloud.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name 日本語の森, handle @nihongonomori2013, id UCVx6RFaEAg46xfAsD2zz16w matches yt.list; Japanese; keywords JLPT N1-N3, EJU. No upload dates on page; RSS feed blocked (robots); one search gave no dated 2026 evidence.

sources.title: Sambon Juku
sources.ja: 三本塾《さんぼんじゅく》
sources.en: Two qualified Japanese teachers give short lessons on single JLPT grammar points, with many example sentences.
sources.tip: When your textbook introduces a grammar point, find the matching short lesson here and copy two of its example sentences into your notes.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name 三本塾, handle @sambonjuku, id UC0ujXryUUwILURRKt9Eh7Nw matches; teachers Akkie and Ayano; mainly Japanese with an English section. No upload dates on page; RSS blocked; search gave nothing dated. speaks kept 'ja' (main language Japanese).

sources.title: Nihongo Benkyou Channel
sources.ja: 日本語《にほんご》 勉強《べんきょう》 チャンネル
sources.en: A teacher named Sato explains N3 to N1 grammar entirely in Japanese, aimed at learners preparing for the JLPT.
sources.tip: Use the long review videos for your level as a checklist of grammar points, then rewatch only the points you could not explain yourself.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name 日本語勉強チャンネル, handle @satojapan, id UCcLwh0oGeEeV73UW5zglzig matches; videos entirely in Japanese, intermediate and above, JLPT N1-N3 grammar. No dates on page; RSS blocked; search gave nothing dated.

sources.title: Arai-sensei's Japanese Channel
sources.ja: あらい 先生《せんせい》 の 日本語《にほんご》 チャンネル
sources.en: A Japanese teacher explains N4 and N3 grammar in simple spoken Japanese, a step from English-medium lessons to Japanese-only ones.
sources.tip: At N4, watch a lesson on grammar you already met in your textbook so you can follow the Japanese explanation, then try a new point.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name あらい先生の日本語チャンネル, id UC8TGHIsPBfnQXK39qXpPKZg matches; About text in English; focus JLPT N3 and N4 grammar. Keigo and 'no English' claims came from a second-hand Tofugu entry, not seen by me, so removed from en. No dates; RSS blocked; search gave nothing dated.

sources.title: Akane's Japanese Class
sources.ja: あかね 的《てき》 日本語《にほんご》 教室《きょうしつ》
sources.en: A language-school teacher talks in Japanese about study, daily life and Japan for learners who want to listen to natural explanations.
sources.tip: At N3, watch with Japanese captions if offered, then once more without; note three new words from each video.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name あかね的日本語教室, handle @Akane-JapaneseClass, id UCh-GhnQ7qDQmS6Bz3pGc1Mw matches; host is a teacher at a Japanese language school; Japanese with some English in description; links to her podcast, Patreon and books. Captions not visible to me, so cc reset to '' (researcher's ja+en was second-hand). No dates; RSS blocked.

sources.title: kt Japanese Learning
sources.en: A Japanese teacher gives lessons on business Japanese, keigo practice, shadowing and everyday phrases that textbooks leave out.
sources.tip: At N3 to N2, do the keigo practice videos aloud: pause before each answer, say yours, then compare with the teacher.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name kt Japanese Learning, handle @satokoyano120, id UCL-4q2Mxgi_DNl_84MsBnww matches; Japanese; business Japanese, keigo, JLPT, shadowing, parenting Japanese; teacher also offers paid private lessons elsewhere (channel itself free, cost 'free'). Page says uploads slow during school breaks. No dates; RSS blocked; search gave nothing relevant.

sources.title: Business Japanese Conversation
sources.ja: ビジネス にほんご かいわ
sources.en: Short workplace conversations for meetings, phone calls, emails, reporting and polite language, shown in kana-only and kanji versions.
sources.tip: At N4 to N3, learn the set phrases for phone calls and reporting to a senior; say each line aloud with the video.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name Business Japanese Conversation (ビジネスにほんごかいわ), handle @shigoto-nihongo, id UCXJCCZWn-K-uZrKdOUKyw8w matches; presenter Shogo Endo; for international professionals; introduction in English, lessons in Japanese with hiragana and kanji versions. speaks kept ja+en because the intro is English; spoken mix not confirmed. No dates; RSS blocked.

sources.title: Meshclass Japanese
sources.en: Teachers explain phrases and grammar for conversation, business, study abroad and the JLPT, mostly in Japanese.
sources.tip: At N3, use the business and formal-phrase videos to build polite set phrases, and leave a request in the comments for topics you need.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name Meshclass Japanese, handle @meshclass, id UCrOSvD4kmjTXzR7ov5zwT-A matches; page in English; topics conversation, business, study abroad, JLPT, anime and manga; keywords N1-N5. No paid courses mentioned on the page, so cost changed to 'free'. 'Mostly Japanese' is from the researcher's second-hand note. No dates; RSS blocked.

sources.title: QuizKnock
sources.en: A Japanese quiz and knowledge group makes puzzle, science and trivia videos for native speakers at natural speed.
sources.tip: Not made for learners: at N2 and above, pick a short quiz video, turn on Japanese captions if they exist, and replay the parts you missed.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name QuizKnock, handle @QuizKnock, id UCQ_MqAw18jFTlBB-f8BP7dw matches; Japanese 'intellectual entertainment' group; description marks its 10th anniversary on 2 October 2026 (dated 2026 evidence). Captions not confirmed. Only the main channel listed.

sources.title: JLPT N1 Nihongo Kikihajime
sources.ja: JLPT N1 日本語《にほんご》 ききはじめ
sources.en: Casual talks about Japan at natural speed with slightly simplified wording, for learners aiming at N1 or study in Japan.
sources.tip: At N2, listen to one talk without captions, write down what you understood, then listen again to check.
sources.notes: Reviewer opened 2026-11-20 via WebFetch: name JLPT N1 日本語ききはじめ, handle @nihongo_kiki_hajime, id UCHaUQg3iUfER81diRQPzq0w (moved from researcher's unverified list; id now found). Japanese; aimed at N1 and graduate-study learners; natural speed, slightly simplified grammar and vocabulary. No dates on page.
